Replay

Claimball session UI

4 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Play againNative match savesBrowser-local Solo saves

Run nix develop --command bash examples/replay_claimball/play.sh. The native menu opens with a name, address, port, and Solo / Host / Join / Watch buttons. Host waits for the first connected player to Start; Solo starts automatically. RCB_PLAYERS sets the minimum player count (one by default in the menu), and RCB_GOALS sets the winning score. Explicit RCB_ROLE launches retain automatic start for existing fixtures. The default port is 49490.

WASD moves, Space kicks, and E spikes. Enter opens chat and captures gameplay input; Escape releases focus while keeping the draft. Chat text is literal. Named observers negotiate support while retaining seat zero. Hold Tab for authoritative player names, teams, scores and round-trip time. A dash means no current ping sample. Departed players remain listed until their seat is reused.

Leave returns to the menu. Rejoining with the same identity retains the seat and match score. Normal native play persists identity at user://replay_claimball_identity and the display name in the adjacent .name file. RCB_PROFILE selects an isolated location. Explicit tokens, bots and RCB_PERSIST=0 bypass profile writes. Malformed saved data is preserved and blocks connection. These files store preferences/identity, not a saved match.

Names and the start command participate in the replayable world. Leader decisions can read roster metadata for outside players without bringing their avatars into the local prediction group. Physics, claim thresholds and remote presentation remain as documented in the main README. Content C3 (0x52434c41494d4233) explicitly distinguishes the new world/action/event schema from C1/C2; no automatic archive conversion is provided.

Party menus and browser sessions now have local RTC acceptance. Steam and public deployment remain work. Fixed native Room recovery is described in migration.md. See the validation results for the retained intermittent observer fault failure.

Play again#

After a completed match, its first connected player can press Play again if enough players remain. The command names the completed round. Guests, observers, in-progress matches, exhausted round counters and stale requests are refused. The new match resets scores, kick/spike/contact totals, ball kickoff, player positions, velocity and cooldowns. Names, teams, connections, seats, match settings, chat history and session action sequencing survive. A departed initialized player keeps its row and is reset for a later return.

This is an addition to the original game's interface. It is a game command inside the existing session, not a disconnect/reconnect operation. Local prediction still contains one avatar plus the ball. Read-only outsider samples stay unchanged until a new authority snapshot arrives. Presentation cuts across round boundaries and ignores old-round kick/spike effects after the new round is confirmed. Gameplay event IDs include the round, so corrections cannot reuse an old match’s effect.

Run nix develop --command bash tests/replay_claimball_ui/round_run.sh for two complete native matches with a host, client and observer. Set REPLAY_CLAIMBALL_ROUND_OUT to a fresh output path to retain the build and receipts.

Native match saves#

Choose a save file in the menu; the default is user://claimball.replay. Save · F5 writes the current authority checkpoint. Only the local authority can save. A failed staging write preserves the previous completed file. A subsequent successful save replaces that file. The button's notice reports completion or a path/write-access problem. F5 is captured while entering chat text.

From a fresh process, Resume solo or Resume host loads that checkpoint with the original host profile. It restores the exact saved frame and opens a newer session epoch. Solo resumes with the host; other saved players are scheduled to leave. In hosted play, their original profiles can rejoin their seats. Round, score, player motion/cooldowns, ball state, roster and match settings come from the checkpoint. The client's prediction group is rebuilt by the existing runner. File resume retires pending commands under the shared default policy; it is not coordinated host migration.

Missing, damaged/incompatible, protected-policy and exhausted-epoch saves are refused before a session opens. The host identity must match the saved local seat. Existing files and identities are kept on rejection. Native file saves do not persist the cosmetic chat history; fresh sessions can exchange named chat again. Browser-local checkpoints now use a separate slot adapter. Provisioned Parties publish through their service; fixed native Rooms disable direct file save/resume. This adds no schema change beyond the existing C3 game version.

Use RCB_SAVE to select a path at launch and RCB_PROFILE for the matching host identity/name profile. Each process can use a separate profile path. Resume solo and Resume host are the supported menu entry points; a dedicated-server resume front door is not part of this increment.

Browser-local Solo saves#

Without a Party service, the browser menu offers Solo, a named save slot and Resume solo. save_slot=pitch is the default query setting. Labels contain 1–48 letters, numbers, dots, dashes or underscores. Storage keys include the personal identity hash, so separate profiles do not share a slot accidentally.

Save waits for an IndexedDB receipt and displays completion or a failure. Leave is blocked while the write is pending. Resume restores the complete saved frame under the same identity in a newer epoch. role=solo&resume=1&save_slot=pitch waits for both identity and slot loading before starting an automatic resume.

Competing tabs use revision checks: a stale tab cannot overwrite the newer save. The UI asks that tab to reload. Malformed checkpoints and identities are preserved and refused; choosing another valid slot permits a new save without changing the bad slot. Browser profile/storage controls outside the game still determine the lifetime of locally stored data.

Party Save/F5 continues to publish through the service and creates no local Solo slot. Browser-local saves, native files and Party publications are separate stores. All use the existing C3 model; this integration does not change its wire schema.
